findings.claim: Objective is final predicted target affinity primary, with validity and strain secondary and coordinate control only; the coordinate representation is predicted endpoint world A features, so all curve values are untyped coordinate proxies rather than physical energies.

The learning/score window is the full observed support [0.0, 0.49] with 50 observed score nodes; recorded affinities were removed and an equal score prior applies, so decoded final affinity is unobserved in this packet.

Across the 20 landmark soft_mass curves, whole-window z magnitudes are small (|z| < 0.65) while first_rate_z and last_rate_z are frequently large and opposite in sign, indicating strong within-window rate contrasts rather than a stationary level target.

landmark_10_soft_mass is the cleanest observed contrast: 14 independent batches, only 2 strong sign conflicts, relative node RMSE 0.51, and a curve that rises from about -0.38 z at t=0 to a mid-window plateau near +0.8 z before declining to about -0.37 z at t=0.49.

No polynomial was accepted for any landmark soft_mass curve (polynomial_accepted false, extrapolation_allowed false), so the observed window cannot be extended beyond [0.0, 0.49] and no absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient is specified by these contrasts.

hypotheses.direction: increase early-window contrast relative to late-window contrast, i.e. favor the rising phase over the declining phase
hypotheses.falsifier: If the landmark_10_soft_mass curve shows no reproducible early-versus-late contrast across independent batches, or if the contrast reverses sign under the same score clock, the hypothesis fails.
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0, 0.49]; no extrapolation
hypotheses.statement: A reward term that tracks the landmark_10_soft_mass coordinate contrast over the observed score window, rather than a fixed absolute level, is supported by the observed rise-then-fall profile with 14 independent batches and few sign conflicts.

hypotheses.direction: emphasize the sign-changing rate contrast over the window instead of a constant level
hypotheses.falsifier: If these features show no consistent sign-changing rate contrast across independent batches, or if whole-window z dominates the rate contrast, the hypothesis fails.
hypotheses.observable: first_rate_z, last_rate_z and whole_window_z of landmark soft_mass curves
hypotheses.scope: global over the observed score window [0.0, 0.49]
hypotheses.statement: Landmark soft_mass coordinates with large opposing first_rate_z and last_rate_z but small whole-window z (e.g. landmark_00, landmark_10, landmark_11, landmark_12, landmark_16) are candidates for time-dependent contrast control rather than stationary level control.

limitations: Decoded final affinity labels are absent from this packet; selection preference and coordinate contrasts are association evidence only and are not evidence of descendant survival or measured final benefit.
Stage profiles and temporal profiles are unavailable; only continuous curves over [0.0, 0.49] were read.
All features are untyped coordinate proxies in predicted endpoint world A; no energy or chemical-interaction interpretation is attached.
No absolute coordinate target or spatial gradient can be derived from these contrasts, and extrapolation beyond the observed window is disallowed.
Current study quality results are withheld from roles, so no claim about generated-molecule quality improvement is made.
